### organizations-account-default-cost-allocation

**Claim.** An account is the default means by which AWS costs are allocated, so separate accounts per business unit or workload group make it easier to report, control, forecast and budget spending; cost allocation tags give finer allocation.

**Write it as.** `default means by which AWS costs are allocated` · `you can apply cost allocation tags`

**Scope.** multi-account strategy.

> "When you require fine-grained cost allocation, you can apply cost allocation tags to individual resources in each of your accounts."
> — [Benefits of using multiple AWS accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/organizing-your-aws-environment/benefits-of-using-multiple-aws-accounts.html)

**Scope.** account removed from an organization.

> "When you remove a member account from the organization, any IAM role that was created to enable access by the organization's management account isn't automatically deleted. If you want to terminate this access from the former organization's management account, then you must manually delete the IAM role."

### organizations-trusted-access-service-acts-on-behalf

**Claim.** Trusted access lets a supported AWS service perform tasks in your organization and its accounts on your behalf by creating service-linked roles; it does not otherwise change the permissions of users or roles.

**Write it as.** `perform tasks in your organization and its accounts` · `create an IAM role called a service-linked role`

**Scope.** AWS services integrated with Organizations.

> "You can use trusted access to enable a supported AWS service that you specify, called the trusted service, to perform tasks in your organization and its accounts on your behalf. This involves granting permissions to the trusted service but does not otherwise affect the permissions for users or roles. When you enable access, the trusted service can create an IAM role called a service-linked role in every account in your organization whenever that role is needed."
> — [Using AWS Organizations with other AWS services](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_integrate_services.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### organizations-wa-root-user-most-privileged

**Claim.** The Well-Architected security pillar says the root user is the most privileged user in an account and in some cases cannot be constrained by security policies; in an organization, secure the management account's root user first, and preventative controls can be placed on member account root users.

**Write it as.** `the most privileged user in an AWS account` · `cannot be constrained by security policies` · `Prioritize securing your management account’s root user`

**Scope.** AWS Well-Architected SEC01-BP02.

> "The root user is the most privileged user in an AWS account, with full administrative access to all resources within the account, and in some cases cannot be constrained by security policies."
> — [SEC01-BP02 Secure account root user and properties](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_securely_operate_aws_account.html)

> "Prioritize securing your management account’s root user, then address your member account root users. The strategy for securing your management account’s root user can differ from your member account root users, and you can place preventative security controls on your member account root users."
> — [SEC01-BP02 Secure account root user and properties](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_securely_operate_aws_account.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### organizations-when-scp-when-rcp

**Claim.** Use an SCP to limit the permissions of IAM principals inside the organization's member accounts; use an RCP to restrict principals outside the organization that request access to resources in member accounts.

**Write it as.** `an SCP when you need to limit permissions` · `RCP when you need to restrict IAM principals`

**Scope.** authorization policies.

> "Use an SCP when you need to limit permissions of IAM principals within your organization's member accounts."
> — [Resource control policies (RCPs)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_rcps.html)

> "Use an RCP when you need to restrict IAM principals that are external to your organization accounts making requests to access resources within your organization’s member accounts."
> — [Resource control policies (RCPs)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_rcps.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.
